findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the rejected set for criterion 6: the forbidden header names (e.g. Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie) and the forbidden value bytes (e.g. CR, LF, NUL) that config resolution must reject with the named error.
evidence: 'Header names and values that could forge authentication or inject protocol bytes are rejected at config resolution with a named error; checked by parametrized tests over the rejected set.'
Approach names only 'Authorization' as an example of a credential-bearing header; no full forbidden-name or forbidden-byte list is given.
Signal (2): implicit acceptance criteria — the size/membership of 'the rejected set' is left to the executor.
findings.finding: Criterion 6 requires rejecting header names/values that 'forge authentication or inject protocol bytes' and is checked 'by parametrized tests over the rejected set', but the plan never enumerates that rejected set. The executor must independently decide which header names are forbidden (only Authorization? also Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie?) and which byte patterns count as protocol injection (CR, LF, NUL, others).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, criterion 6; Child decomposition, configuration child
scenarios: Two implementers ship different forbidden-name lists; one blocks Cookie, the other does not.
A CRLF-in-value test passes on one implementation and is absent on another.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the configuration child a concrete list: reject the header names Authorization/Proxy-Authorization/Cookie (case-insensitive) and any value containing CR, LF, or NUL, raising a single named error.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fallback when a substituend is absent (unset ${env:VAR}; ${run:ticket_id} on the ticket-less code-review path; a run with no minted trace_id): whether the header is dropped, the value empties, or resolution errors, on every gate surface.
evidence: code_review/sidecar.py:4: 'code review reviews a DIFF, which has no ticket. So this emit takes an EXPLICIT target_ticket' and target_ticket defaults to None (shim.py:127)
Plan lists code-review implicitly under 'gate LLM calls' (delivery child) yet AC4 names only plan-review and completion surfaces, leaving ${run:ticket_id} undefined for the ticket-less gate
T8(d): an unspecified fallback for an incomplete sub-step — the substitution step cannot complete when the substituend is missing
findings.finding: No fallback is specified for a substituend that is absent at resolution time: an unset `${env:VAR}`, or `${run:ticket_id}` on the code-review diff-only path which has no ticket. The plan does not say whether an absent value yields an empty string, drops the header, or raises a config error.
findings.location: delivery child ("owns ${run:...} interpolation") and configuration child ("${env:...} interpolation"); AC2 and AC3
scenarios: A code-review run whose diff has no rebar-ticket trailer resolves `${run:ticket_id}` against nothing
An operator references `${env:GATEWAY_KEY}` but the variable is unset in the run environment

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion covering the documentation deliverable (operator recipe + security guidance), or state why the documentation child intentionally has no in-session-verifiable criterion.
evidence: 'A documentation child records the operator-facing recipe and security guidance, and depends on the delivery child.'
No acceptance criterion references docs, a recipe, or security guidance.
E1: 'every described deliverable has a covering criterion (no orphans, no uncovered work).'
findings.finding: The documentation child is a described deliverable ('records the operator-facing recipe and security guidance') but no acceptance criterion covers it. Criteria 1-6 all map to the configuration, run-correlation, and delivery children; none verifies the documentation output.
findings.location: Child decomposition, documentation child; Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: The documentation child ships nothing verifiable and there is no criterion to fail if the recipe is omitted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a criterion such as: 'The operator-facing header/correlation recipe and its security guidance (credential-displacement, redaction) are documented; checked by a doc artifact present under docs/ referencing the headers config surface.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile 26ae's delivery gate with the intermediary condition it cites: either gate on `base_url or provider in gateway-provider-names` (matching capabilities.py:622) or explicitly state and justify why gateway/* providers are excluded from header delivery.
evidence: 26ae Approach: 'Headers are attached only when cfg.base_url is set.'
26ae Approach: 'This reuses the condition src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:554 already treats as "an intermediary is present" when it flips provenance tier to best_effort.'
capabilities.py:622 shows that condition is actually `"best_effort" if (base_url or via_gateway)` — i.e. base_url OR gateway-provider membership, not base_url alone.

capabilities.py:575-582 / _GATEWAY_PROVIDER_NAMES (gateway/anthropic, gateway/bedrock, gateway/google-cloud, gateway/groq, gateway/openai) 'are live ... and carry NO base_url, because the gateway URL is resolved inside pydantic-ai from its own env/API key.'
Parent Context: 'This epic serves the deployment where the gateway, not rebar, feeds the backend.'
container pairing: parent + 26ae-041f-dcc4-4279/6cd0-0786-4de8-415e/98b6-efa8-bf15-4760/ee8a-6355-2e8f-4da3
findings.finding: Child 26ae gates header delivery solely on cfg.base_url being set, but the parent's target topology includes gateway/* providers that carry no base_url, so those gateway runs receive no correlation headers even though they are exactly the intermediary deployment the epic targets.
scenarios: An operator runs gate calls through a gateway/anthropic (or other gateway/* provider) with no explicit base_url; correlation/observability headers are silently never sent, so the gateway still receives anonymous calls — the exact problem the epic set out to fix.
26ae acknowledges only the Bedrock-inert consequence, not this gateway/* class, so the mismatch between its cited condition and its actual gate goes unremarked.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 26ae's delivery condition to match the provenance intermediary condition (base_url OR gateway-provider membership), or add an explicit acknowledged-consequence and criterion documenting that gateway/* providers without base_url are intentionally excluded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the extra_headers capability empirically: add a verification (test or documented manual check) that OpenAIChatModel and AnthropicModel — rebar's two actual model classes — emit configured extra_headers onto the outbound request, citing pydantic-ai #6843 as the reason doc-level 'Supported by' is insufficient.
evidence: Plan quote: 'It is upstream-supported (pydantic_ai/settings.py, documented for OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Google and others)'

Retrieved GitHub issue pydantic/pydantic-ai#6843: 'ModelSettings.timeout and ModelSettings.extra_headers both list xAI under Supported by:, but models/xai.py never reads either one. Both are silently dropped.'
Rebar builds OpenAIChatModel (src/rebar/llm/providers.py:276) and AnthropicModel (src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:181,190) — the specific classes whose extra_headers wiring must be confirmed

The delivery child's criterion 3 test 'captures headers across the calls of one simulated run' but a simulated/TestModel path does not prove the real OpenAI/Anthropic model classes emit the header on the wire
findings.finding: The plan states extra_headers is 'upstream-supported (documented for OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Google and others)' as a settled capability, but upstream pydantic-ai issue #6843 documents that extra_headers is silently dropped by at least one provider (xAI) despite being listed as 'Supported by' — so 'documented as supported' does not guarantee the headers reach the wire. The plan resolves the capability by doc citation, not by verifying delivery on rebar's two concrete model classes (OpenAIChatModel, AnthropicModel).
findings.location: Approach → 'ModelSettings.extra_headers beats patching httpx clients' bullet
scenarios: An operator configures ${run:trace_id} headers, tests pass against the simulated run, but a future/edge pydantic-ai provider path drops extra_headers and gateway traces silently stay anonymous — the exact failure this epic exists to fix
findings.suggested_fix: In the delivery child, strengthen criterion 3's test to assert headers on a captured outbound httpx request (e.g. via a MockTransport / recording client) for both the OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic paths, rather than only a TestModel-simulated run, and note pydantic-ai #6843 as the rationale.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the exact value set `${run:operation}` resolves to (e.g. the gate operation ids review-plan / verify-completion / review-code) so the delivery child and its tests have a defined vocabulary.
evidence: Plan lists three run tokens but only trace_id has a defined format ('32-hex lowercase id') and lifecycle ('minted at the gate run boundaries')
operation is never tied to a concrete value set; the codebase gate surfaces are review-plan, verify-completion, and review-code, but the plan neither names these nor states the token yields them
T8(a): a value vocabulary referenced by a structured-substitution contract but never defined
findings.finding: The `${run:operation}` substitution token is referenced as part of the per-run value vocabulary but the set of values it resolves to is never enumerated, so a delivery executor cannot implement it and an operator cannot write a header value that keys off it.
findings.location: Approach section ("rebar-supplied per-run values (${run:trace_id}, ${run:ticket_id}, ${run:operation})") and the delivery child ("owns ${run:...} interpolation")
scenarios: Operator configures `X-Gateway-Op: ${run:operation}` and cannot predict the emitted string
Delivery-child implementer must guess the operation label source
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach or delivery-child text, state the closed value set for ${run:operation} (the gate operation identifiers) and where it is sourced from at the run boundary.

evidence: src/rebar/llm/config.py: 6cd0-0786-4de8-415e & ee8a-6355-2e8f-4da3 (no ordering edge)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (against pydantic-ai's per-provider docs/source) that `ModelSettings.extra_headers` actually reaches the wire on each provider path the plan claims (OpenAI/httpx, Anthropic, Bedrock, Google), or narrow the supported-provider claim to the OpenAI-compatible gateway path that is the epic's actual target and mark other providers as unsupported/best-effort.
evidence: Plan quote: 'It is upstream-supported (`pydantic_ai/settings.py`, documented for OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Google and others)'
`pydantic_ai.settings.ModelSettings` resolves EXISTS (Verified); the base field family is real
No repo usage of `extra_headers` exists (search returns no matches) — this is a NEW surface for rebar
capabilities.py:700-703 shows Bedrock goes via `pydantic_ai.models.bedrock` which imports botocore, a non-httpx transport — header delivery there is Partially-verified/Unverified
Evidence class: extra_headers on the OpenAI/httpx path = Partially-verified; Bedrock/Google delivery = Unverified
findings.finding: The plan asserts `ModelSettings.extra_headers` is upstream-supported and delivered to the wire uniformly across 'OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Google and others', but the specific per-provider delivery surface is unverified for the non-httpx providers — Bedrock in particular routes through boto3/botocore (capabilities.py:701 notes bedrock imports botocore), where an httpx-style extra request header may not thread through.
findings.location: Approach — '`ModelSettings.extra_headers` beats patching httpx clients' bullet
scenarios: An operator on a Bedrock or Google model configures correlation headers expecting them on gate calls, but headers are silently dropped because the provider transport ignores `extra_headers`.
